nodes.name: ApiKeyAuthenticationHandler
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Api.ApiKeyAuthenticationHandler">
    <summary>
    Authenticates a request via the <c>X-Api-Key</c> header against <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ApiKeyStore"/>, as an
    alternative to the interactive JWT login flow (<see cref="T:Connector.Api.Endpoints.AuthEndpoints"/>) for a "dedicated
    API user" — a machine calling a specific endpoint directly (e.g. an external system triggering a saved
    export preset). Registered as its own scheme ("ApiKey") alongside the default JWT Bearer scheme, so
    only endpoints that opt in via <c>RequireAuthorization(policy => policy.AddAuthenticationSchemes(...))</c>
    accept it — every other endpoint keeps requiring a JWT exactly as before.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: Permissions

<member name="T:Connector.Api.Authorization.Permissions">

    permission, plus the admin-only areas that aren't grantable at all (Connect, Users, Permissions). The keys are

    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: Normalize
nodes.doc:
<member name="M:Connector.Api.Authorization.Permissions.Normalize(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.String})">
    <summary>

    permission can't grant anything), and every permission adds its group's <c>.view</c> permission, since
    e.g. editing an export job you can't open makes no sense.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: RolePermissionStore
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Api.Authorization.RolePermissionStore">
    <summary>

    (<c>{ "User": ["exportJobs.view", ...] }</c>) and cached in memory, since it is checked on nearly every request.
    The cache is dropped on every save, so an Admin's change applies to the next request rather than after the
    affected users' tokens expire. Singleton: reads go through a fresh scope's <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ExportLogDbContext"/>.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: GetAsync

</member>

nodes.name: SaveAsync

nodes.name: ExportDefinitionEndpoints
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Api.Endpoints.ExportDefinitionEndpoints">
     <summary>
     CRUD, manual trigger, test, preview, and run history for
     <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ExportDefinitionEntity"/>: the generic, named, tree-based replacement for the legacy single
     export mapping (see knowledge/pipeline/export-definitions-2.0.md). This is the surface an external
     program uses to configure a saved export once and trigger it later via a single authenticated
     POST — <c>POST /api/export-definitions/{id}/run</c> returns the built artifact bytes directly.
    
     Deliberately does not reuse <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ExportRunEntity"/>/<see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.FileSystemExportSink"/>/four-eyes
     release: those model the legacy CI-to-vendor staging contract (sequence numbers, physical staging
     folder, approval workflow), which don't apply to generic exports. A run here is synchronous
     request/response plus one <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ExportDefinitionRunEntity"/>
     history row — no separate storage or delivery mechanism is introduced.
     </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ValidateRequestAsync
nodes.doc:
<member name="M:Connector.Api.Endpoints.ExportDefinitionEndpoints.ValidateRequestAsync(Connector.Api.ExportDefinitionRequest,Connector.Infrastructure.ExportLogDbContext,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32})">
    <summary>
    Validates a create/update request: name, root table, output format, cron schedule, the
    IntegrationKey/ContractVersion pair (including uniqueness among enabled definitions), the root filter and
    the whole node tree via ValidateNode. Returns the normalized RootNode on success (null on failure) alongside the error, so callers store
    exactly the tree that was validated instead of re-normalizing (or re-validating null-prone raw input) a
    second time. `internal` rather than `private` so Connector.Integration.Tests can exercise the
    IntegrationKey/ContractVersion save-time guardrails directly, mirroring
    ImportDefinitionEndpoints.ValidateRequestAsync's own visibility.
    </summary>
</member>

    Recursive validator over the ExportNode tree: depth guard, identifier-safety, GDPR denylist, and

</member>

     class rather than separate classes so the `internal` methods each already exposes to

     live introspected ERP schema, or one that's a primary key, identity/computed column, or foreign key —
     and rejects any node whose <c>OnMissingChild</c> is <c>"insert"</c> outright, since child-row creation

    exercise it directly against the in-memory Sqlite <c>LocalDb</c> fixture — this never opens an ERP
    connection, unlike <see cref="M:Connector.Api.Endpoints.ImportDefinitionEndpoints.ValidateRequestAsync(Connector.Api.ImportDefinitionRequest,Connector.Infrastructure.ExportLogDbContext,Connector.Core.DataSources.IDataSourceProviderResolver,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32})"/>, so it needs no Postgres testdb.

nodes.doc: Connection parameters for the configured ERP data source. Provider-agnostic by design: says which (resolved via ) interprets the rest of these fields — a relational source (/ ) uses //, an HTTP API source (/ ) uses instead. See knowledge/architecture/data-source-configuration.md for the full design and back-compat contract. Init-only, so a non-relational source doesn't need to fake a Host/Port/Database it doesn't have. Back-compat: every property defaults the way a JSON payload missing it must deserialize — to (the enum's 0 value), / to "" — so a stored AppSettings row without a type key deserializes as an equivalent PostgreSql config. nodes.name: NativeSqlQuery
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DataSources.NativeSqlQuery">
    <summary>
    Provider-native SQL text (plus optional named parameters) for
    <see cref="M:Connector.Core.DataSources.IDataSourceProvider.ExecuteNativeAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig,Connector.Core.DataSources.NativeSqlQuery,System.Threading.CancellationToken)"/>. The database-neutral counterpart is
    <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DataSources.SourceQuery"/>.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Two producers exist: a provider's own compiler for <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DataSources.SourceQuery"/> (e.g.
    <c>Connector.Infrastructure.DataSources.PostgreSql.PostgreSqlQueryCompiler</c>), and
    <c>DynamicExportService</c>'s export builders (JSON object/array aggregation trees, rendered through the
    provider's SQL dialect), which the neutral model cannot express yet — see knowledge/architecture/source-query-model.md §5. The provider only executes this
    text and materializes rows generically; it never parses it. Nothing in <c>Connector.Core</c> builds one.
    <para><see cref="P:Connector.Core.DataSources.NativeSqlQuery.ReturnNativeText"/>: when true, every value comes back as the backend's own text rendering
    of it (e.g. PostgreSQL's <c>2024-03-15 10:11:12.5</c>, <c>t</c>, <c>{1,2}</c>) instead of the provider's
    default stringification, and <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DataSources.QueryResultColumn.DataType"/> names the backend type to interpret it
    by. The export tree engine uses this to render typed JSON values in C# exactly as the database would have.</para>
    </remarks>
</member>

    compiler may assume any query that passes is safe to turn into native syntax (every name it quotes is one
    the schema itself reported).

    success, or a sanitized, user-facing <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DataSources.TestConnectionResult.Error"/> on failure — never both. A provider must never
    let a raw exception (which can echo connection-string/credential detail) reach <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DataSources.TestConnectionResult.Error"/>
    unsanitized.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ExportManifest
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.Domain.ExportManifest">
    <summary>
    Accompanies every export file. Lets the recipient verify integrity and detect gaps without a
    return channel — the sequence number exposes gaps (e.g. a jump from #41 to #43).
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ExportProducer
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.Domain.ExportProducer">

nodes.name: ExportPackage
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.Domain.ExportPackage">

</member>

nodes.name: ImportManifest
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.Domain.ImportManifest">

    mirroring <see cref="!:FileSystemExportSink"/>'s outbound contract. No <c>SequenceNumber</c>: vendor
    confirmations don't arrive 1:1 per export run, so gap detection doesn't apply — the SHA-256 checksum
    alone covers file integrity. Which saved <c>ImportDefinition</c> a file targets is carried inside the
    data file's own <c>ImportEnvelope</c> (its <c>definition</c> field), not here — the manifest's only job
    is integrity.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ManifestSignature
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.Domain.ManifestSignature">

    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ExportMappingRelation

nodes.name: ExportMappingNestedGroup

<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportMappingNestedGroup">

nodes.name: ExportJsonMetadataField

<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportJsonMetadataField">

nodes.name: ExportJsonWrapperConfig
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportJsonWrapperConfig">

    field naming. Null on <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportMappingConfig.JsonWrapper"/> preserves the legacy flat envelope.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ExportMappingConfig
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportMappingConfig">
    <summary>The complete mapping config for one source table, including field remaps and relation flattening.
    <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportMappingConfig.NestedGroups"/> and <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportMappingConfig.JsonWrapper"/> are JSON-export-only and additive: CSV/Excel export

</member>

nodes.name: ExportMappingJson
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportMappingJson">
    <summary>
    Deserializes <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportMappingConfig"/> stored as <c>AppSetting</c> JSON, repairing configs saved
    before relations gained a <c>Fields</c> list, <c>Delimiter</c>, and relation-level <c>FlattenStrategy</c>:
    System.Text.Json leaves a missing property at its type default — <see langword="null"/> for the string and

    C# enum + <c>JsonStringEnumConverter</c>.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: FieldTransform
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.FieldTransform">

nodes.name: FieldDataType
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.FieldDataType">
    <summary>Discriminator values for <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.FieldMapping.DataType"/>, used to coerce a scalar
    value at read time (e.g. a SQL <c>::text</c>/<c>::numeric</c> cast) ahead of format-writer serialization.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: FieldMapping
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.FieldMapping">
    <summary>Value-shaping for one <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNode"/> of kind <see cref="F:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNodeKind.ScalarField"/>:

    data type used for format-writer coercion.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ExportNode
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNode">
    <summary>
    One node in a recursive export tree. Generalizes <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportMappingNestedGroup"/> (which only
    covers "object"/"array" nesting for JSON output) to also represent the root and plain scalar columns,
    so a single tree — walked by one query builder and honored by every format writer (CSV/Excel/JSON) —
    replaces the old parallel <c>Fields</c>/<c>Relations</c>/<c>NestedGroups</c> shapes. <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNode.Children"/>
    lets root/object/array nodes nest arbitrarily deep; a scalar-field node has no children.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ExportNodeJson
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNodeJson">
    <summary>
    Deserializes an <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNode"/> tree stored as JSON (on <c>ExportDefinitionEntity.RootNode</c>),
    backfilling missing properties the same way <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportMappingJson"/> does for the legacy mapping
    shape: System.Text.Json leaves a missing property at its type default rather than the value an older
    saved tree implied, which would otherwise crash every consumer that dereferences it. Every read of a
    persisted <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNode"/> tree must go through this instead of a raw
    <see cref="M:System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Deserialize``1(System.String,System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions)"/> call.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: NormalizeMapping
nodes.doc:
<member name="M:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNodeJson.NormalizeMapping(Connector.Core.DynamicExport.FieldMapping)">
    <summary>Public so <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNodeJson"/> can reuse the same
    backfill for the <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.FieldMapping"/> it shares verbatim, instead of duplicating it.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ExportRecordSelection
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportRecordSelection">
    <summary>
    Optional, server-derived root selection: the configured correlation column and caller-supplied values.
    The SQL compiler binds the values as parameters and intersects them with the saved root filter.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ExportDefinitionShape
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ExportDefinitionShape">
    <summary>
    The subset of a persisted <c>ExportDefinitionEntity</c> (Connector.Infrastructure) that
    <see cref="M:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportMappingSuggestion.SuggestFrom(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ExportDefinitionShape},Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportSampleShape)"/> needs. A plain Core-level record because Connector.Core
    has no dependency on Connector.Infrastructure. The caller loads it from
    <c>ExportLogDbContext.ExportDefinitions</c> and deserializes <c>RootNode</c> via <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNodeJson"/>
    first — this type does no I/O of its own.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ImportSampleShape
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportSampleShape">
    <summary>
    The inbound sample a suggestion is built from: the provenance pair read off the sample
    <c>ImportEnvelope</c> (null when the sample carries no <c>provenance</c> block, which yields no
    suggestion, never an error) and the top-level JSON key names of one sample record, used only for the
    best-effort candidate-field scan.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ImportMappingCandidateField
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportMappingCandidateField">
    <summary>
    One best-effort candidate field offered alongside the deterministic root prefill — unchecked/disabled by
    default. The operator must explicitly enable it, and it still goes through the schema-aware
    <c>AllowedWritableColumns</c> validator before it can be saved as writable; matching a key name back to
    the same underlying column is a name-based heuristic, not a proven contract.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ImportMappingSuggestionResult
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportMappingSuggestionResult">
    <summary>Result of <see cref="M:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportMappingSuggestion.SuggestFrom(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ExportDefinitionShape},Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportSampleShape)"/>: the deterministic root prefill
    (the export's correlation key, so both sides are the same field by contract) plus the best-effort
    candidate list.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ImportMappingSuggestionMiss
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportMappingSuggestionMiss">
    <summary>
    Why <see cref="M:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportMappingSuggestion.Evaluate(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ExportDefinitionShape},Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportSampleShape)"/> found nothing to suggest — every gate the lookup
    can silently fail on, named so the API layer (which has the entity `Name`s <see cref="!:Evaluate"/>
    itself never sees, per Core's no-Infrastructure-dependency rule) can turn a miss into an operator-facing
    explanation instead of a flat "no match." Ordered by how far the sample got.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ImportMappingSuggestionOutcome
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportMappingSuggestionOutcome">
    <summary>Full outcome of <see cref="M:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportMappingSuggestion.Evaluate(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ExportDefinitionShape},Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportSampleShape)"/>: exactly one of
    <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportMappingSuggestionOutcome.Result"/>/<see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportMappingSuggestionOutcome.Miss"/> is set.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ImportMappingSuggestion
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportMappingSuggestion">
    <summary>
    An authoring convenience that suggests a starting <c>ImportDefinition</c> from a paired,
    provenance-tagged <c>ExportDefinition</c> (see knowledge/pipeline/import-mapping-presets.md). Pure: no
    I/O, no side effects. Never called by <c>Connector.Infrastructure.ImportNodeWalker</c>/<c>ImportWorker</c>
    at processing time — a matched pair only saves the operator typing at authoring time; it is never a
    trust or routing mechanism.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: SuggestFrom
nodes.doc:
<member name="M:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportMappingSuggestion.SuggestFrom(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ExportDefinitionShape},Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportSampleShape)">
    <summary>
    Finds the (at most one, per the save-time uniqueness constraint) enabled export among
    <paramref name="candidates"/> whose (IntegrationKey, ContractVersion) equals <paramref name="sample"/>'s
    pair, then builds the suggestion from it. Returns null — never throws — whenever there is nothing to
    suggest. Thin wrapper over <see cref="M:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportMappingSuggestion.Evaluate(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ExportDefinitionShape},Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportSampleShape)"/> that drops the miss reason.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: Evaluate
nodes.doc:
<member name="M:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportMappingSuggestion.Evaluate(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ExportDefinitionShape},Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportSampleShape)">
    <summary>
    Same lookup as <see cref="M:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportMappingSuggestion.SuggestFrom(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ExportDefinitionShape},Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportSampleShape)"/>, but on a miss names *which* gate stopped it
    (<see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportMappingSuggestionMiss"/>) instead of collapsing every reason into a bare null —
    the API layer uses this to turn "no match found" into an operator-facing explanation (a candidate
    exists but is disabled, or exists but has no CorrelationKeySourceField, vs. no candidate at all).
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ImportNodeKind
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNodeKind">
    <summary>Discriminator values for <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNode.Kind"/> — same set as
    <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNodeKind"/>, kept as its own type since
    <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNode"/> intentionally doesn't merge into <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNode"/> (see that
    record's doc comment for why).</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: OnMissingChildPolicy
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.OnMissingChildPolicy">
    <summary>Discriminator values for <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNode.OnMissingChild"/>: what happens to an
    object/array child node whose <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNode.JoinKey"/> doesn't resolve to an existing row.
    Only meaningful for <see cref="F:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNodeKind.Object"/>/<see cref="F:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNodeKind.Array"/> nodes —
    root rows are match-only unless the definition opts into <see cref="F:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.UnmatchedRootPolicy.Insert"/>.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: UnmatchedRootPolicy
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.UnmatchedRootPolicy">
    <summary>Discriminator values for <c>ImportDefinitionEntity.UnmatchedRootPolicy</c>: what happens to an
    inbound record whose correlation key matches no root row. <see cref="F:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.UnmatchedRootPolicy.Insert"/> creates the row, and is only
    accepted on a definition with an <c>IntegrationKey</c> (a connector-to-connector contract, never a vendor
    file).</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ImportNode
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNode">
    <summary>
    One node in a recursive import tree — the write-side mirror of <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNode"/>: same
    shape (root/scalar-field/object/array, arbitrarily nested via <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNode.Children"/>, reusing
    <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.FieldMapping"/> verbatim for value coercion), walked in the opposite direction.
    Deliberately its own type rather than merged into <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNode"/>: <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNode.SourceKey"/>
    reads from inbound JSON where <c>ExportNode.SourceField</c> reads from SQL,
    <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNode.TargetColumn"/> writes to SQL where <c>ExportNode.TargetKey</c> writes to JSON, and
    <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNode.OnMissingChild"/> is a write-only policy with no export-side analogue — forcing both
    into one type would mean nullable fields that are meaningless half the time.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ImportNodeJson
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNodeJson">
    <summary>
    Deserializes an <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNode"/> tree stored as JSON (on
    <c>ImportDefinitionEntity.RootNode</c>), backfilling missing properties the same way
    <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNodeJson"/> does: a tree saved before a property existed must not crash every
    consumer that dereferences it. Every read of a persisted <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNode"/> tree must go
    through this instead of a raw <see cref="M:System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Deserialize``1(System.String,System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions)"/> call.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ImportFieldDiff
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportFieldDiff">
    <summary>One column-level change a walked row would make: the value currently stored in the ERP versus
    the (already <see cref="!:FieldMapping"/>-coerced) value the inbound record supplies. Only emitted when the
    two differ — an unchanged column contributes no entry, since "diff" means "what would actually change."
    <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportFieldDiff.OldValue"/> is not just display data: the commit-time concurrency check uses it as the
    conditional write's <c>expectedOldValue</c> — an <c>UPDATE</c> guarded on the target column still matching
    this value — so a row whose ERP state moved on since this diff was computed is caught, not silently
    overwritten.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ImportRowStatus
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportRowStatus">
    <summary>Outcome of matching one inbound record's correlation key against <c>RootTable</c>/
    <c>RootMatchColumn</c>. <see cref="F:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportRowStatus.Rejected"/> and <see cref="F:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportRowStatus.Quarantined"/> both mean "excluded from the
    accepted set" (see <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.UnmatchedRootPolicy"/>) — kept distinct here so a review UI can show which
    policy fired, not just that the record didn't match; <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportPlanBuilder"/> folds both into
    <c>ImportRunEntity.RejectedCount</c>, since that entity has no separate quarantine counter. <see cref="F:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportRowStatus.Invalid"/>
    is for a record that isn't even a well-formed row to evaluate a policy against (e.g. not a JSON object) —
    distinct from <see cref="F:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportRowStatus.Rejected"/>, which means the row parsed fine but its correlation key didn't
    match anything. <see cref="F:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportRowStatus.Accepted"/> covers both "matched/changed" and "matched/unchanged" — a row
    whose target fields already equal the incoming values is
    still <see cref="F:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportRowStatus.Accepted"/> here, just with an empty <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportRowResult.Fields"/> diff;
    <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportPlanBuilder"/> is what splits that back out into <c>ChangedCount</c>/
    <c>UnchangedCount</c>.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ImportChildResult
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportChildResult">
    <summary>One <see cref="F:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNodeKind.Object"/>/<see cref="F:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNodeKind.Array"/> child's resolution
    result for one parent row: whether its <c>JoinKey</c> resolved to an existing related row, and — for
    <see cref="F:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNodeKind.Object"/> children only, where "the related row" is unambiguous — the field-level
    diff for that row. <see cref="F:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNodeKind.Array"/> children only get the existence check: no
    <c>ImportDefinition</c> writes to a child table, and matching individual array items to individual
    existing rows needs a per-item identity key the data model doesn't have.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ImportRowResult
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportRowResult">
    <summary>One inbound record's full walk result: whether its root row was matched, the field-level diff if
    so, and the resolution of every object/array child under it. <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportRowResult.CorrelationValue"/> is kept even for
    a rejected/quarantined row (null only when the record had no readable correlation value at all) so a review
    UI can show which vendor record failed to match, not just a bare count.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ImportWalkResult
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportWalkResult">
    <summary>Full result of walking one inbound JSON file against one <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNode"/> tree: a
    diff-only shape for preview/review. The persisted write list (<c>PlanJson</c>) is built from it by
    <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportPlanBuilder"/>.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ImportValidationException
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportValidationException">
    <summary>Thrown for a structural problem with the saved <c>ImportDefinition</c> itself (a <c>TargetColumn</c>
    outside <c>AllowedWritableColumns</c>, a missing root match field, malformed inbound JSON) — never for an
    individual record's data, which is reported via <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportRowResult"/> instead. Distinguishing the
    two matters to the caller: a thrown exception means "this run cannot proceed at all," while
    a rejected/quarantined row is a normal, expected part of a successful walk.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ImportPlanOperation
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportPlanOperation">
    <summary>
    One column-level write the commit step makes: the value observed on the ERP row when the
    plan was built (<see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportPlanOperation.ExpectedOldValue"/>) and the value to write in its place. This is the same
    value <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportFieldDiff.OldValue"/> already carries — the field is renamed here, not
    re-derived, to make its second job explicit: <c>ImportRunReleaser</c>'s (Connector.Infrastructure)
    conditional <c>UPDATE ... WHERE ... IS NOT DISTINCT FROM @expectedOldValue</c> guard
    uses this exact value, so a row whose ERP state moved on since staging is excluded from the commit rather
    than silently overwritten. <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportPlanOperation.CorrelationValue"/> is carried for audit/troubleshooting only — the
    commit itself addresses the row via <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportPlanOperation.Table"/>/<see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportPlanOperation.KeyColumn"/>/<see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportPlanOperation.KeyValue"/>,
    which are always <c>RootTable</c>/<c>RootMatchColumn</c>/the matched root row's
    correlation value (see <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportPlanBuilder"/> for why child-table writes aren't emitted here).
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ImportPlan
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportPlan">
    <summary>
    The persisted write protocol for one <c>ImportRunEntity</c> (Connector.Infrastructure):
    <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportPlan.Operations"/> is the structured, versioned list <c>ImportRunReleaser</c> commits from, and the
    only authoritative source for what a release actually writes — a UI diff or audit-log line is a read
    projection of this, never a second independently-computed shape. The five counts mirror
    <c>ImportRunEntity</c>'s own (<see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportPlan.MatchedCount"/> = <see cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportPlan.ChangedCount"/> +

Only root-row fields become operations. diffs (an object-kind child like maintenancePlan) stay visible in the walk result for the review UI, but are never turned into a write here: AllowedWritableColumns covers root-entity columns only. nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Infrastructure.DataSources.ISqlDialect">
    <summary>
    The SQL syntax that differs between relational backends, as far as this codebase actually uses it — not a
    general-purpose SQL abstraction (no SQL framework, no AST, no ORM). Generic query
    builders (<see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.DynamicExportService"/>, <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportNodeWalker"/>, <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunReleaser"/>)
    assemble statements from plain ANSI keywords (<c>SELECT</c>/<c>FROM</c>/<c>WHERE</c>/<c>AND</c>/<c>AS</c>)
    plus these members; everything else is a dialect's job. Implementations:
    <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.DataSources.PostgreSql.PostgreSqlDialect"/> and <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.DataSources.MariaDb.MariaDbDialect"/>. See
    knowledge/architecture/sql-dialect.md.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Members past the first three exist because a concrete builder needs them today, not speculatively: string
    literals and a string aggregate for the legacy flat export, text casts and a batched key match for the export
    tree engine's per-level child queries, rendering a native text value as JSON for that engine's C#-side tree
    assembly, and a null-safe comparison for the import releaser's optimistic-concurrency guard.
    Every member returns a SQL fragment; callers must only pass it identifiers from a known schema/config,
    expressions built by this dialect, or values they escape through <see cref="M:Connector.Infrastructure.DataSources.ISqlDialect.QuoteStringLiteral(System.String)"/>.
    </remarks>
</member>

nodes.name: PostgreSqlJsonValues
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Infrastructure.DataSources.PostgreSql.PostgreSqlJsonValues">
    <summary>
    Turns a PostgreSQL value in its text output format into the JSON value PostgreSQL's own <c>to_json</c> would
    produce for it — so the export tree engine can assemble JSON in C# that is identical to what the database
    would build with <c>json_build_object</c>. Follows <c>to_json</c>'s type categories:
    <list type="bullet">
    <item><c>smallint</c>/<c>integer</c>/<c>bigint</c>/<c>real</c>/<c>double precision</c>/<c>numeric</c> →
    a JSON number with the exact same digits (<c>NaN</c>/<c>Infinity</c> stay strings, as in Postgres);</item>
    <item><c>boolean</c> → <c>true</c>/<c>false</c>; <c>json</c>/<c>jsonb</c> → embedded as JSON;</item>
    <item><c>date</c> → unchanged; <c>timestamp</c>/<c>timestamptz</c> → ISO 8601 with a <c>T</c> separator
    and a <c>±HH:MM</c> offset;</item>
    <item>arrays → JSON arrays, element by element (nested arrays nest);</item>
    <item>everything else (text, uuid, time, interval, enums, …) → a JSON string of the text as-is.</item>
    </list>
    Assumes the server's default <c>DateStyle</c> (ISO), which is what makes date/timestamp text ISO-shaped.
    Composite (row) types and types with a custom cast to json aren't special-cased — they come out as
    strings; no exported column in this codebase uses either.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ServiceNowSchemaReader
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Infrastructure.DataSources.ServiceNow.ServiceNowSchemaReader">
    <summary>
    Reads ServiceNow's table/field metadata through the ordinary Table API — <c>sys_db_object</c> (tables and their
    <c>super_class</c> inheritance) and <c>sys_dictionary</c> (fields) — into the same <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DataSources.SourceSchema"/>
    shape the SQL providers return. Needs read access to those two tables (e.g. the <c>personalize_dictionary</c>
    role), not admin; like every Table API read, the result only contains what the account's ACLs allow.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Mapping: a table's fields are its own plus every ancestor's (e.g. <c>incident</c> inherits <c>task</c>'s);
    <c>sys_id</c> is the primary key; a <c>reference</c> field is a foreign key to <c><referenced table>.sys_id</c>
    — so <c>incident.assignment_group</c> is a relation to <c>sys_user_group</c> like any SQL foreign key; a field
    is nullable unless <c>mandatory</c>.
    </remarks>
</member>

<member name="T:Connector.Infrastructure.DataSources.ServiceNow.ServiceNowTableApiProvider">
    <summary>

    ServiceNow read over its REST Table API, behind the same interface as the SQL providers — callers see
    <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DataSources.SourceSchema"/>, <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DataSources.SourceQuery"/> and <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DataSources.QueryResult"/>, never HTTP. Not an
    <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.DataSources.ISqlDataSourceProvider"/>: there is no SQL to run, so <see cref="M:Connector.Infrastructure.DataSources.ServiceNow.ServiceNowTableApiProvider.ExecuteNativeAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig,Connector.Core.DataSources.NativeSqlQuery,System.Threading.CancellationToken)"/> and the
    SQL-rendering export builders refuse it with <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DataSources.UnsupportedDataSourceException"/>.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Joins run in C#: after the root read, each join reads the joined table with <c>column IN (parent values)</c> in
    batches of <see cref="F:Connector.Infrastructure.DataSources.ServiceNow.ServiceNowTableApiProvider.JoinKeyBatchSize"/> — one request per batch and page, never one per root record — and
    matches rows by value, as an inner or left equi-join. ServiceNow returns every value as a string and an empty
    field as <c>""</c>; the provider reports both an empty and a missing field as <c>null</c>.
    </remarks>
</member>

nodes.name: ExecuteExportNodeQueryAsync
nodes.doc:
<member name="M:Connector.Infrastructure.DynamicExportService.ExecuteExportNodeQueryAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.IDataSourceProvider,Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig,System.String,Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNode,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlySet{System.String},Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportRecordSelection)">
    <summary>
    Runs one <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNode"/> tree (rooted at <paramref name="rootTable"/>) and returns one JSON tree
    per root row — the generic successor to <see cref="M:Connector.Infrastructure.DynamicExportService.ExecuteNestedJsonQueryAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.IDataSourceProvider,Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig,Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportMappingConfig,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlySet{System.String})"/> that also covers plain
    scalar columns, so it is the only query path <see cref="M:Connector.Infrastructure.DynamicExportService.BuildExportNodeAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.IDataSourceProvider,Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig,System.String,Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNode,System.String,System.String,System.DateTimeOffset,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlySet{System.String},Connector.Infrastructure.ExportProvenance,System.String,Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportRecordSelection)"/> needs regardless of
    output format. The database returns plain rows, one query per tree node; the tree is assembled in C#
    (<see cref="M:Connector.Infrastructure.DynamicExportService.ExecuteTreeQueryAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.IDataSourceProvider,Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig,Connector.Infrastructure.DynamicExportService.TreePlan,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Threading.CancellationToken,Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportRecordSelection)"/>). Every scalar is a JSON string of its <c>::text</c> form (or JSON
    null), an array node with no matches is <c>[]</c>, an object node with no match is <c>null</c>, and an
    object node with several matches fails the export. GDPR enforcement is two layers: a denylisted <see
    cref="P:Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportNode.SourceField"/> is excluded from the SELECT list entirely (so it never leaves the
    database, and — since this is re-evaluated against the *current* denylist on every run — a
    definition saved before a field was denylisted is covered too, not just newly-saved ones), plus
    <see cref="M:Connector.Infrastructure.DynamicExportService.StripGdprFieldsRecursive(System.Text.Json.Nodes.JsonNode,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlySet{System.String})"/>'s output-key match as a second, independent layer of
    defence-in-depth.
    </summary>
    <param name="provider">Data source the queries run against; also picks the SQL dialect.</param>
    <param name="dsConfig">Connection settings for provider.</param>
    <param name="rootTable">Table the tree's root rows come from.</param>
    <param name="root">The export tree to run.</param>
    <param name="ct">Cancels the queries.</param>
    <param name="limit">Maximum root rows (previews and test runs), or null for all rows.</param>
    <param name="gdprDenylist">Source fields to exclude; defaults to GdprDeniedFields.</param>
</member>

    Runs <paramref name="def"/> once: inserts a Running history row, builds the export from its node tree
    against the configured connection (GDPR denylist and provenance tag applied), then finalizes the row as

    its manifest are also written to the staging folder, and a failed write fails the run. A failure is returned
    as <c>Error</c> with <c>Built</c> null rather than thrown; only cancellation propagates.

</member>

<member name="P:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunEntity.DefinitionSnapshotJson">
    <summary>The full <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportDefinitionEntity"/> (RootTable, RootMatchColumn, RootNode,
    AllowedWritableColumns, UnmatchedRootPolicy), serialized exactly as it stood at staging time.
    <see cref="P:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunEntity.ConfigVersion"/> names *which* version; this field *is* that version, frozen — so an
    approver reviewing this run is never looking at a diff computed against a definition that's
    since been edited.</summary>
</member>

    checksum alone covers file integrity.
    Unique together with <see cref="P:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunEntity.ImportDefinitionId"/> so the same vendor file
    can never be staged twice.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: PlanJson

<member name="P:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunEntity.PlanJson">
    <summary>A structured, versioned list of write operations (table, row-key, column, old value,
    new value, expected old value) — the write-side source of truth for this run. A UI diff is a
    read-only projection of this, never a second authoritative shape. Reused
    verbatim by both the review UI and the commit step so preview and commit can never
    disagree about what a row means.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: StagedConnectionFingerprint
nodes.doc:
<member name="P:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunEntity.StagedConnectionFingerprint">
    <summary>The ERP connection's identity (host/port/database — no credentials, see
    <see cref="M:Connector.Infrastructure.DynamicExportService.ConnectionFingerprint(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig)"/>) at the moment this run was staged.
    <see cref="M:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunReleaser.ReleaseAsync(Connector.Infrastructure.ExportLogDbContext,Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunEntity,System.String,System.String,Connector.Infrastructure.AuditService,Connector.Core.DataSources.IDataSourceProviderResolver,System.Threading.CancellationToken)"/> compares it with the *current* connection setting, so an
    approval given for a plan built against target A can't be committed against a target B the connection
    setting was changed to in the meantime. Null for runs staged without a fingerprint — release skips the
    check for those.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ImportNodeWalker
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportNodeWalker">
    <summary>
    The write-side mirror of <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.DynamicExportService"/>'s tree walker: parses an inbound
    <c>ImportEnvelope</c> against a saved <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNode"/> tree, and produces a field-level diff per
    accepted row plus a rejected-row list — with zero write capability. Every method here only ever issues SQL
    <c>SELECT</c>s; the conditional <c>UPDATE</c> path is <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunReleaser"/>, which commits the
    plan built from this same walk result (<see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportPlanBuilder"/>), so preview and commit can never
    disagree about what a row means.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: WalkAsync
nodes.doc:
<member name="M:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportNodeWalker.WalkAsync(Connector.Infrastructure.DataSources.ImportConnection,Connector.Infrastructure.ImportDefinitionEntity,Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNode,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)">
    <summary>
    Walks <paramref name="inboundJson"/> (an <c>ImportEnvelope</c> — <c>schemaVersion</c> + <c>records</c>)
    against <paramref name="root"/>, matching each record's correlation key against
    <paramref name="definition"/>'s <c>RootTable</c>/<c>RootMatchColumn</c> and computing a field-level diff
    for every match. Throws <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportValidationException"/> for a problem with the saved definition
    or the inbound file itself (never for one bad record — see that type's doc comment); an individual
    record's correlation mismatch is reported via <see cref="T:Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportRowResult"/>, not an exception.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: FindMatchField
nodes.doc:
<member name="M:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportNodeWalker.FindMatchField(Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNode,System.String)">
    <summary>Finds the root's own scalar-field child mapped to <paramref name="rootMatchColumn"/> — the
    JSON property the walker reads to get each record's correlation value. Only ever looked up among the
    root's DIRECT children: the correlation key names a column on <c>RootTable</c> itself, never a nested
    related table. Public so the save-time validator (<c>Connector.Api.Endpoints.ImportDefinitionEndpoints</c>)
    can reuse this exact lookup rather than re-implementing it, instead of only discovering a missing
    match field at run time.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ValidateWritableColumns
nodes.doc:
<member name="M:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportNodeWalker.ValidateWritableColumns(Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNode,Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNode,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlySet{System.String})">
     <summary>
     Checks every scalar-field node in the tree (root and nested, excluding <paramref name="matchField"/>,
     which is read for matching only and is never written) against <paramref name="allowedColumns"/> and,
     defensively, the GDPR denylist — a saved definition that somehow targets a column outside its own
     allowlist must never be trusted silently. Returns the offending column names rather than throwing
     directly, so the caller can build one aggregate error message instead of failing on only the first
     violation found.
    
     <para>Not schema-aware: rejecting a primary key, identity/computed column, or foreign key as a
     <c>TargetColumn</c> is the save-time validator's job. This run-time re-check is list membership plus
     the GDPR denylist.</para>
     </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ParseRecords
nodes.doc:
<member name="M:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportNodeWalker.ParseRecords(System.String)">
    <summary>Parses the inbound file as the canonical <c>ImportEnvelope</c>: a top-level
    JSON object carrying <c>schemaVersion</c> and a <c>records</c> array. <c>schemaVersion</c> is checked
    first, before any record is touched — a missing or unrecognized version is a definition/file-level
    problem (there's no per-record recovery from "I don't understand this file's shape"), so it throws
    rather than guessing at a shape.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: CollectSelectColumns
nodes.doc:
<member name="M:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportNodeWalker.CollectSelectColumns(Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNode,System.String)">
    <summary>Column list for a root-row (or child-row) fetch: the match/join column itself, every direct
    scalar-field <c>TargetColumn</c> (so the diff has an "old value" to compare against), and every direct
    relation child's <c>SourceJoinKey</c> (so a grandchild's own fetch has the parent value it needs) —
    de-duplicated since the same column can legitimately serve more than one of those roles.</summary>
</member>

nodes.doc:
<member name="M:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportNodeWalker.ResolveChildAsync(Connector.Infrastructure.DataSources.ImportConnection,Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNode,System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary{System.String,System.String},System.Text.Json.Nodes.JsonObject,System.Threading.CancellationToken)">

nodes.name: ImportRunReleaser
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunReleaser">
    <summary>
    Commits an approved <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunEntity"/>
    to the ERP under the same Operator/Approver four-eyes contract the export release flow already enforces —
    the write-side counterpart to <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ExportDefinitionRunner"/>. <see cref="M:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunReleaser.ReleaseAsync(Connector.Infrastructure.ExportLogDbContext,Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunEntity,System.String,System.String,Connector.Infrastructure.AuditService,Connector.Core.DataSources.IDataSourceProviderResolver,System.Threading.CancellationToken)"/> and
    <see cref="M:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunReleaser.RejectAsync(Connector.Infrastructure.ExportLogDbContext,Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunEntity,System.String,Connector.Infrastructure.AuditService,System.Threading.CancellationToken)"/> take an already-loaded <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunEntity"/> (the caller — an API
    endpoint — owns fetching it and checking its <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunStatus"/>) and finalize it; neither
    method opens its own DbContext scope, matching every other run-mutating helper in this codebase
    (<see cref="M:Connector.Infrastructure.ExportDefinitionRunner.ExecuteAsync(Connector.Infrastructure.ExportDefinitionEntity,Connector.Infrastructure.ExportLogDbContext,Connector.Core.DataSources.IDataSourceProviderResolver,System.String,System.Boolean,System.Nullable{System.Int32},Connector.Infrastructure.FileSystemExportSink,System.Threading.CancellationToken,Connector.Core.DynamicExport.ExportRecordSelection)"/>, the inline export release handler).
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ReleaseAsync
nodes.doc:
<member name="M:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunReleaser.ReleaseAsync(Connector.Infrastructure.ExportLogDbContext,Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunEntity,System.String,System.String,Connector.Infrastructure.AuditService,Connector.Core.DataSources.IDataSourceProviderResolver,System.Threading.CancellationToken)">
    <summary>
    Applies <paramref name="run"/>'s persisted <c>PlanJson</c> to the ERP: one conditional <c>UPDATE</c> per
    row — every column that row's plan changes, guarded by every one of that row's
    captured expected-old-values in a single <c>WHERE</c> clause, so a row commits all its changed columns
    or none of them, never half. Zero affected rows means the row's ERP state moved on since staging; that
    row is excluded, counted in <see cref="P:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunEntity.ConflictCount"/>, and left untouched — it does
    not fail the run. An unrelated failure (a thrown exception — e.g. a constraint
    violation) rolls back everything committed so far in this call and marks the run
    <see cref="F:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunStatus.Failed"/>, matching the "no silent partial success" rule already enforced on
    the export side. Caller (an endpoint, in <c>Connector.Api</c>) must have already validated
    <paramref name="operatorName"/>/<paramref name="approver"/> for the four-eyes distinctness check and
    that <paramref name="run"/>.Status is <see cref="F:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunStatus.PendingReview"/>.
    </summary>
</member>

<member name="M:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunReleaser.InsertRowAsync(Connector.Infrastructure.DataSources.ImportConnection,System.Data.Common.DbTransaction,System.ValueTuple{System.String,System.String,System.String},System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportPlanOperation},System.Threading.CancellationToken)">

<member name="M:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunReleaser.RejectAsync(Connector.Infrastructure.ExportLogDbContext,Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunEntity,System.String,Connector.Infrastructure.AuditService,System.Threading.CancellationToken)">

nodes.name: ImportWorker
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportWorker">
    <summary>
    A sibling of <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ExportWorker"/> that polls an <c>inbound/</c> staging folder instead of writing to
    one. Every vendor-supplied file dropped there is manifest-checked, idempotency-checked against
    <c>(ImportDefinitionId, Sha256Checksum)</c>, walked by <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportNodeWalker"/> against the
    <c>ImportEnvelope</c> — the <c>definition</c> field says which saved <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportDefinitionEntity"/> to
    use — and staged as an <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunEntity"/> at <see cref="F:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunStatus.PendingReview"/>, with
    <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportDefinitionEntity"/> frozen onto it as <see cref="P:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunEntity.DefinitionSnapshotJson"/>.
    This worker never writes to the ERP itself — that's <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportRunReleaser"/>'s job, once a human
    approves the staged plan.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: PollOnceAsync
nodes.doc:
<member name="M:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportWorker.PollOnceAsync(System.Threading.CancellationToken)">
    <summary>One polling pass over <see cref="F:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportWorker._inboundPath"/> — public so a test can drive it directly
    against a real inbound directory and testdb, without waiting out the timer loop. Never throws: a
    broken file or a scope/DB failure is logged and the rest of the pass continues, matching the
    <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ExportWorker"/>/<see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ExportDefinitionWorker"/> resilience convention.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ProcessFileAsync
nodes.doc:
<member name="M:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportWorker.ProcessFileAsync(System.String,System.String,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)">
    <summary>
    Stages one inbound data file as a PendingReview import run. The file needs a manifest whose SHA-256 matches
    and a JSON envelope naming an enabled import definition; it is then walked and planned against the
    configured connection, the run is saved and audited, and the file moves to processedDir. Anything invalid is
    quarantined to rejectedDir with an audited reason; a file already staged for the same definition and
    checksum is audited as a duplicate and moved to processedDir. A file that can't be read yet (still being
    copied) is left for the next poll.
    </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ExtractDefinitionName
nodes.doc:
<member name="M:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportWorker.ExtractDefinitionName(System.Text.Json.Nodes.JsonNode)">
    <summary>Reads the <c>definition</c> property off the top-level <c>ImportEnvelope</c> object — the
    only envelope field this worker needs beyond what <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportNodeWalker"/>
    already reads (<c>schemaVersion</c>/<c>records</c>) — without otherwise validating the envelope's
    shape; <see cref="M:Connector.Infrastructure.ImportNodeWalker.WalkAsync(Connector.Infrastructure.DataSources.ImportConnection,Connector.Infrastructure.ImportDefinitionEntity,Connector.Core.DynamicImport.ImportNode,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)"/> is what actually enforces <c>schemaVersion</c> and
    <c>records</c>. Pure and DB-free so it's unit-testable without a database or filesystem. Returns null
    for anything that isn't a well-formed envelope with a non-blank string <c>definition</c>.</summary>
</member>

nodes.name: SessionRevocationStore
nodes.doc:
<member name="T:Connector.Infrastructure.SessionRevocationStore">
     <summary>
     JWT revocation: stores, per username, the earliest a JWT for that user may have been issued to still be
     considered valid. Every token carries its own issued-at claim (see <c>AuthEndpoints</c>), and
     <c>Program.cs</c>'s <c>OnTokenValidated</c> handler rejects any token issued before that cutover. Backed by
     the encrypted-at-rest <see cref="T:Connector.Infrastructure.AppSettingEntity"/> key/value store rather than a dedicated table.
    
     Self-service only: a user can revoke their own sessions (<c>POST /api/auth/revoke-my-sessions</c>). There
     is no admin action to revoke another user's sessions, since there is no role model to authorize it.
     </summary>
</member>

nodes.name: ExportNodeTreeEditor
