nodes.doc: <member><summary>Schedule picker: presets (Manual/Hourly/Daily/Weekly) plus an advanced free-text cron field. modelValue is the raw ExportDefinition.Schedule (a 5-field cron string, or null for manual-only) — this never invents a second source of truth for it.</summary></member>

nodes.name: FieldPickerTable
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Shared by RelationCard and NestedGroupEditor — both need an identical checkbox+rename table over "columns of a related table", differing only in which property holds the rename (relations call it targetField, nested groups call it targetKey). `targetProp` picks that property type-safely per caller instead of forcing the two mapping shapes to match.</summary></member>

nodes.name: FlatPreviewTable
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Read-only grid of flat preview rows (numbered, one column per export column, '—' for a missing value), with a note when the preview was capped.</summary><param name="columns">Column names, in display order.</param><param name="rows">Rows to show, keyed by column name.</param><param name="totalCount">Total rows the preview returned; the cap note shows when it exceeds max.</param><param name="max">The preview row cap, shown in the cap note.</param></member>

nodes.name: GdprDenylistEditor
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Settings editor for the GDPR denylist: source fields that are never exported. Add or remove field names, then save; the new list applies to the next export or preview.</summary><param name="initialFields">The currently stored denylist, used as the starting list.</param></member>

nodes.name: IcdExcludedFieldsList
parameters: fields: { erpSource: string; reason: string; detail: string; tag: string }[]

nodes.name: ImportAllowedColumnsEditor
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>This is the primary safety boundary of the whole import feature: a saved mapping can never write outside this explicit allowlist, checked against the live schema at save time. Deliberately its own component, visibly separate from the tree, so it's never something an operator can miss while scrolling past field rows.</summary><param name="usedColumns">TargetColumn values the tree currently references (excluding the root match field) — used only
to flag ones missing from the allowlist below; the tree itself is never edited from here.</param></member>

nodes.name: ImportDefinitionBasicFields
nodes.doc:
<member><param name="rootTableLocked">Disables the root-table picker once children reference it — changing tables out from under an
already-built tree would silently invalidate every TargetColumn/RelatedTable in it.</param></member>

nodes.name: ImportDefinitionPreviewPanel
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>Preview runs POST .../preview — parses + walks + plans a sample inbound file against this saved definition with zero persistence (no ImportRunEntity, nothing written to the ERP). Run instead posts to .../runs, which stages a real ImportRunEntity at PendingReview the same way the inbound/ folder watcher would — the parent view owns that call so it can refresh run history / open the review dialog.</summary><param name="plan">Result of the last preview: per-record matches and planned changes, or null before the first preview.</param><param name="loading">True while a preview request runs.</param><param name="error">Error from the last preview, or null.</param><param name="running">True while the parent stages a real run from the sample.</param><param name="rootNode">Optional: the saved definition's field tree, used only for the client-side "unmapped field" hint
below — never sent anywhere, never affects what Preview actually runs.</param></member>

nodes.name: ImportDefinitionRunControls
nodes.doc: <member><summary>The import-side analogue of ExportDefinitionRunControls.vue — deliberately narrower: there's no "Test against live connection" here (an import definition has no query to sanity-check). Staging a real run (manual file select or the inbound/ folder watcher) and previewing a sample file both live on ImportDefinitionPreviewPanel.vue instead, since both act on the same pasted/selected JSON it already owns.</summary><param name="definition">The definition being edited; saved as-is, and updated in place with the server's response.</param></member>

nodes.name: ImportDefinitionRunsTable
nodes.doc: <member><summary>The import-side analogue of ExportDefinitionRunsTable.vue: same per-definition run-history shape, but carries the full count breakdown (changed/unchanged/inserted/rejected/conflicted/ invalid) instead of a bare record count, and a Review action on PendingReview rows — the entry point into ImportRunReviewDialog.vue's four-eyes commit flow.</summary></member>

nodes.name: ImportDiffValue
nodes.doc: <member><summary>One old/new value cell's contents, shared by both columns of ImportPlanDiffTable.vue — split out purely to keep that table's own template under fallow's complexity gate, not because either side has behavior of its own beyond the null/empty check and which style applies.</summary></member>

nodes.name: ImportMappingSuggestionPanel
nodes.doc: <member><summary>"Create from export": the New Import Definition flow's other starting point besides "Start blank." A dedicated step rather than reusing ImportDefinitionPreviewPanel.vue's paste-a-sample affordance verbatim — that panel drives POST .../{id}/preview against an *already-saved* definition's live ERP connection, which doesn't exist yet here. This mirrors its paste-JSON UX instead, wired to the suggestion lookup rather than a plan diff.</summary></member>

nodes.name: ImportNodeTreeEditor
nodes.doc: <member><summary>The write-side mirror of ExportNodeTreeEditor.vue: same recursive-editor idea, built against ImportNode instead of ExportNode. Two differences follow directly from the data model, not from UI taste: there's no Filter input (ImportNode has no such field — every matched row is in scope, filtering happens at the correlation-key match, not here), and OnMissingChild has no picker at all — only "reject" is permitted (the save-time validator rejects "insert" outright), so offering a choice that always fails server-side would be actively misleading.</summary><param name="nodes">The nodes at this level; edited in place (add/remove/change), with `dirty` emitted after each change.</param><param name="contextTable">Table this level's columns are written to: the root table, or the parent node's related table.</param><param name="availableTables">Introspected source tables and their columns, used for column pickers and suggested relations.</param><param name="depth">Nesting level (0 at the root): indents the level and hides "add" once MAX_NESTED_DEPTH is reached.</param></member>

nodes.name: ImportPlanDiffTable
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Shared by ImportDefinitionPreviewPanel.vue (a sample-file preview) and ImportRunReviewDialog.vue (a staged run's four-eyes review) — both need the same "one row's changed fields, grouped by CorrelationValue" rendering of a plan's operations as a field-level diff. PlanJson is the write-side source of truth; this component only ever displays operations handed to it, never recomputes anything.</summary></member>

nodes.name: ImportPlanSummaryBadges
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Split out of ImportDefinitionPreviewPanel.vue purely to keep that panel's own template under fallow's complexity gate. isStale means the sample textarea has been edited since `plan` was computed (Preview is an explicit, manual action — it never reruns just because the text changed), so the count badges below dim and a banner explains why they may no longer match what's on screen.</summary></member>

nodes.name: ImportRunCountSummary
nodes.doc: <member><summary>The count breakdown for one import run — pulled out of ImportRunReviewDialog.vue purely to keep that file's already-branchy template (loading/error/pending/terminal states) from growing further; this piece itself has almost no branching of its own. `insertCount` is optional and only shown when non-zero: rows created under UnmatchedRootPolicy "insert" (connector-to-connector imports).</summary></member>

nodes.name: ImportRunOutcome
nodes.doc: <member><summary>The read-only "what happened" summary for a Released/Rejected/Failed import run — the ImportRunReviewDialog.vue counterpart to its own pending-review Operator/Approver form, pulled out for the same reason as ImportRunCountSummary.vue: keeping the dialog's own template from growing another branch.</summary><param name="operatedBy">User who released or rejected the run, or null.</param><param name="approvedBy">Second user who approved a release, or null (rejections need no approver).</param><param name="releasedAt">When the run was released (ISO 8601), or null.</param><param name="errorMessage">Why the release failed, or null.</param></member>

nodes.name: ImportRunReviewDialog
nodes.doc: <member><summary>The import run review/diff view: reuses ReleaseDialog.vue's Operator/Approver form pattern, extended with the full count breakdown and a field-level diff of the matched/changed rows PlanJson actually carries — a run's plan is the write-side source of truth, so this dialog only ever displays it, never recomputes its own.</summary><param name="runId">Import run to load when the dialog opens; null renders nothing to review.</param></member>

nodes.name: ImportUnmappedFieldsWarning
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Split out of ImportDefinitionPreviewPanel.vue purely to keep that panel's own template under fallow's complexity gate — see findUnmappedRootFields (lib/importPreviewHints.ts) for what this actually warns about. Renders nothing when there's nothing to warn about, so the caller can drop it in unconditionally alongside the (mutually exclusive) "looks like an exported job file" alert.</summary></member>

nodes.name: JobRowActions
nodes.doc: <member><summary>The per-row actions of the Export Jobs and Import Jobs lists: open (Edit, or View without the edit permission), then Test, Duplicate and Delete (with confirm), each shown only when the parent allows it.</summary><param name="to">Route of the job's edit page.</param><param name="canEdit">Whether the user may change the job, which labels the link Edit rather than View.</param><param name="testing">True while that action runs for this row.</param></member>

nodes.name: NestedGroupEditor
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>Self-referencing recursive component. Vue 3 SFCs can implicitly reference themselves by filename, but defineOptions makes the self-registration explicit and independent of the file staying named exactly "NestedGroupEditor.vue".  Template complexity is intentionally left unsplit here: this component supports arbitrary nesting depth, so its "children" block recurses into itself — pulling that block into a separate file would just import this file right back, a circular dependency fallow itself flags as worse than the complexity it'd save. The field-row and field-picker sections are already extracted (see FieldPickerTable.vue); this is what's left after that.</summary><param name="group">The nested group being edited; mutated in place, with `dirty` emitted after each change.</param><param name="availableTables">Introspected source tables and their columns, used for the related-table and field pickers.</param><param name="depth">Nesting level (0 at the top): child groups can't be added once MAX_NESTED_DEPTH is reached.</param><param name="siblings">The full list of groups at this same level (including this one) — used to detect a
duplicate export key among siblings, which would otherwise silently overwrite a key
in the exported JSON. Defaults to just this group when no siblings are known.</param></member>

nodes.name: NestedGroupsSection
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Pure structural preview of the JSON shape being built — target keys, object vs. array, and nesting only, no live data. Lets someone see the tree they're building without running a real export first.</summary></member>

nodes.name: PermissionsSettings
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Admin-only Settings → Permissions: one card per menu item with a checkbox per permission, deciding what the User role may see and do. Ticking any permission ticks the item's "View" too, and unticking "View" clears the rest, mirroring how the server normalizes the set. Applies on the users' next click after saving.</summary></member>

nodes.name: PresetsToolbar
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Named export-mapping presets for the legacy mapping screen: load the saved presets, apply one (emits `apply` with its config), save the current mapping under a name ("Save As…", overwriting a same-named preset), or delete the selected preset.</summary><param name="canSave">False until the mapping has a source table; saving is refused with an inline hint until then.</param><param name="getConfig">Returns the current mapping config to store when saving a preset.</param></member>

nodes.name: PreviewTable
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>Preview panel for the legacy export mapping: shows loading, errors, an empty state, or the first 20 records, as nested JSON or a flat table depending on the mapping. Emits `refresh` to re-run the preview.</summary><param name="preview">Result of GET /api/pipeline/preview, or null before the first load.</param><param name="loading">True while the preview request runs.</param><param name="error">Error from the request itself (e.g. backend unreachable), or null. Query errors arrive inside preview
instead.</param></member>

nodes.name: RelationCard
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Collapsible editor for one flattened relation in the legacy mapping: related table, join columns, which related fields to include, and how multiple matches are flattened (strategy and delimiter). Can be removed or converted into a nested group.</summary><param name="relation">The relation being edited; mutated in place, with `dirty` emitted after each change.</param><param name="relatableTables">Tables that can be joined, with their columns.</param><param name="selectedTableColumns">Columns of the mapping's source table, offered for the source-side join column.</param></member>

nodes.name: ReleaseDialog
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Four-eyes release for a pending export run: a button that opens a dialog where a second user enters their credentials to approve. The approver can't be the signed-in operator. Emits `released` on success.</summary><param name="seqNo">Sequence number of the export run to release.</param></member>

nodes.name: ResetPasswordDialog
nodes.doc: <member><summary>An Admin sets a new password for `username` (open while it is non-null). The server signs that user out everywhere.</summary></member>

nodes.name: RunDetailTable
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Read-only table of an export run's details: sequence, extraction time, record count, SHA-256 (copyable), file name, and release and delivery information.</summary><param name="run">The export run to show.</param></member>

nodes.name: RunHistoryFrame
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Shared shell of the per-definition run-history tables (ExportDefinitionRunsTable.vue, ImportDefinitionRunsTable.vue): heading with Refresh, loading/error states, the empty message, and the table with its header row. Callers supply only the body rows, through the default slot.</summary><param name="title">Heading shown above the table, e.g. "Run History".</param><param name="columns">Header cells, in order; `numeric` right-aligns the column.</param><param name="loading">True while the runs are being fetched; shows "Loading…" and spins the Refresh button.</param><param name="error">Load error to show instead of the table, or null.</param><param name="empty">True when there are no runs; shows `emptyText` instead of the table.</param><param name="emptyText">Message shown when `empty` is true.</param></member>

nodes.name: SchedulerSettingsForm
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Settings form for the nightly managed export: run time (UTC), how many days staged export files are kept, and the output format. Takes effect on the next export cycle.</summary><param name="config">The currently stored scheduler settings, used as the form's initial values.</param></member>

nodes.name: SkipRunForm
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Form on a pending or failed export run's detail page for skipping it, with an optional reason for the audit log. Emits `skipped` on success.</summary><param name="seqNo">Sequence number of the export run to skip.</param></member>

nodes.name: StatusBadge
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Data-driven instead of a switch/ternary chain: a status maps to one (icon, color) pair here, and every consumer — export runs, export/import definition runs, import-run four-eyes review — funnels through the same table rather than each growing its own branch.</summary></member>

nodes.name: ThemeToggle
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Icon-only — the text labels ("Light"/"Auto"/"Dark") took up nav space the top bar doesn't have to spare. Each button keeps an aria-label/title so the meaning isn't icon-only for screen readers or on hover.</summary></member>

nodes.name: UserMenu
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Export Jobs and Import Jobs moved to top-level nav pills in App.vue — this menu now holds only the connector-configuration screens that don't need to be always-visible. Only the screens the signed-in user may open (their route's access rule, see router/index.ts).</summary></member>

nodes.name: UserRowActions
nodes.doc: <member><summary>The actions on one Settings → Users row. Your own row offers only the password reset: the server refuses changing your own role or deleting yourself.</summary><param name="self">Whether this row is the signed-in Admin.</param><param name="busy">True while a change to this user runs.</param></member>

nodes.name: UsersSettings
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Admin-only Settings → Users: every login with its role, plus adding a user, switching a role, resetting a password and deleting a user. The server refuses changes to your own role or account and to the last Admin.</summary></member>

nodes.name: Badge
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Generic status/count pill. Consolidates the ad-hoc "rounded-full px-2 py-0.5 text-xs" spans that were hand-rolled per view (count summaries, preview panels, ...) — StatusBadge stays the icon+label variant for run/import statuses specifically; this is the plain no-icon pill for everything else.</summary></member>

nodes.name: Button
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Standard button in four visual variants. While `loading`, it shows a spinner (hiding the `icon` slot) and is disabled; the default slot is the label.</summary><param name="variant">Visual style: primary (default) and danger are solid main actions, secondary and ghost are flat.</param><param name="type">Native button type; 'button' by default so it never submits a form by accident.</param><param name="disabled">Disables the button.</param><param name="loading">Shows a spinner in place of the icon and disables the button while an action runs.</param></member>

nodes.name: ConfirmAction
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>De-duplicates the "click Delete → inline Confirm/Cancel" pattern repeated across run-controls panels and definition list rows. Renders as a fragment (no wrapping element) so it drops straight into whatever flex row the trigger button already lived in — `confirming` swaps the trigger slot for a prompt + confirm/cancel pair in place, matching how each call site already laid things out.</summary><param name="busy">True while the confirmed action runs: shows a spinner on Confirm (button variant) or disables it
(link variant).</param><param name="prompt">Question shown next to the buttons in the button variant; defaults to "Delete permanently?".</param><param name="confirmLabel">Label of the confirm control.</param><param name="cancelLabel">Label of the cancel control.</param><param name="variant">'button' renders confirm/cancel as full Button components with a text prompt (toolbar-style
actions); 'link' renders them as bare text links (table-row actions).</param></member>

nodes.name: EmptyState
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Shared "nothing here yet" block for lists/tables — replaces the one-off `<div class="text-text-secondary text-sm mt-4">No … yet.</div>` lines duplicated across views with a consistent, slightly more prominent treatment, while staying just as easy to drop in.</summary><param name="icon">Optional icon shown above the title.</param><param name="title">Main message, e.g. "No export jobs yet".</param><param name="description">Optional secondary line under the title.</param></member>

nodes.name: FieldShell
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Layout shared by Input and Select: label (with a required marker), the control in the default slot, then either the error or the help text underneath. The ids let the control reference its label, help and error for accessibility.</summary><param name="id">Id of the control in the slot; the label's `for` points at it.</param><param name="helpId">Id given to the help text, for the control's aria-describedby.</param><param name="errorId">Id given to the error message, for the control's aria-describedby.</param><param name="label">Label text; omitted when not set.</param><param name="required">Adds a required marker (*) to the label.</param><param name="helpText">Hint shown under the control when there is no error.</param><param name="error">Error message shown under the control, replacing the help text.</param></member>

nodes.name: HelpTooltip
nodes.doc: <member><summary>A small "?" affordance for explaining a non-obvious field, section, or concept in place — click (or Enter/Space) to open a short explanation, Escape or an outside click to dismiss. Content is plain semantic markup in the default slot (p/strong/code/ul); :slotted() below gives it consistent typography so call sites don't have to repeat utility classes every time.</summary><param name="label">Accessible name for the trigger button — say what it explains, e.g. "About contract versions".</param><param name="title">Optional bold heading at the top of the panel.</param><param name="align">Which edge of the trigger the panel lines up with: left (default), right or center.</param></member>

nodes.name: Input
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Labelled text input bound with v-model (string or number), built on FieldShell. Wires aria-invalid and aria-describedby to the error or help text; the id is generated when not given.</summary><param name="id">Id for the input; generated when omitted.</param><param name="label">Label shown above the input.</param><param name="helpText">Hint shown under the input when there is no error.</param><param name="error">Error message shown under the input; also marks it aria-invalid.</param><param name="type">Native input type; 'text' by default.</param><param name="placeholder">Placeholder text.</param><param name="disabled">Disables the input.</param><param name="required">Marks the field required, natively and with a * on the label.</param><param name="autocomplete">Native autocomplete hint, e.g. 'username'.</param><param name="maxlength">Maximum length in characters.</param><param name="min">Minimum value for number inputs.</param><param name="max">Maximum value for number inputs.</param></member>

nodes.name: Modal
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Accessible dialog shown while v-model:open is true: traps Tab focus inside, closes on Escape (and optionally on a backdrop click), and returns focus to the previously focused element when it closes. Default slot is the body; the `footer` slot holds the actions.</summary><param name="title">Heading shown with a close button; also labels the dialog. No header is rendered when omitted.</param><param name="closeOnBackdrop">Whether clicking the backdrop closes the dialog; true by default.</param></member>

nodes.name: PageHeader
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Consolidates the "eyebrow + <h1> + trailing actions" block repeated (with minor drift) at the top of every list/detail view, so it converges on the --text-page-title token instead of each view picking its own text-xl/arbitrary-value heading size.</summary></member>

nodes.name: SectionHeader
nodes.doc: <member><summary>The sub-heading counterpart to PageHeader — for the <h2>-level section titles ("Presets", "Allowed Writable Columns", ...) that sit above a card or toolbar within a view, converged on the --text-section-heading token.</summary></member>

nodes.name: Select
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Labelled native select bound with v-model, built on FieldShell; the options go in the default slot. Wires aria-invalid and aria-describedby like Input.</summary><param name="id">Id for the select; generated when omitted.</param><param name="label">Label shown above the select.</param><param name="helpText">Hint shown under the select when there is no error.</param><param name="error">Error message shown under the select; also marks it aria-invalid.</param><param name="disabled">Disables the select.</param><param name="required">Marks the field required, natively and with a * on the label.</param></member>

nodes.name: useBranding
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>Shared branding state. First call kicks off the load; later calls (including after saving new
branding in Settings) reuse the same refs and can force a fresh `reload()`.</summary></member>

nodes.name: loadCurrentUser
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Reloads the current user; resolves to null when the session is no longer valid.</summary></member>

nodes.name: canAccess
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Whether the current user may open a route with this access rule.</summary></member>

nodes.name: canOpen
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>Whether the current user may open a resolved route: its `meta.access`, or `meta.createAccess` when its :id
param is "new" (the page creates something).</summary></member>

nodes.name: useSaveStatus
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>The saving/saveStatus/saveMessage triad duplicated identically across several definition/settings
save forms — factored out once a third copy (SchedulerSettingsForm.vue) pushed the clone past
fallow's duplicate-detection threshold.</summary></member>

nodes.name: useTheme
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Shared app-wide theme preference: 'light' | 'dark' follow a manual choice, 'system' follows prefers-color-scheme.</summary></member>

nodes.name: useToasts
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>App-wide toast queue for confirming saves/deletes/etc. — a reactive singleton in the same
module-scope-ref style as useTheme, rendered by the single <ToastHost/> mounted in App.vue.</summary></member>

nodes.name: withSourceType
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>Switches the source type. The port follows the new type's default unless the user typed their own, and a
TLS mode the new type doesn't offer (MariaDB has no "Allow") falls back to the default.</summary></member>

nodes.name: formFromStored
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Form state for a stored connection. The password is never part of GET responses, so it stays empty.</summary></member>

nodes.name: toConnectionConfig
nodes.doc: <member><summary>The POST body: only the fields the chosen source type uses, everything else null.</summary></member>

nodes.name: validateConnectionForm
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Per-field messages for missing/invalid required fields of the chosen source type.</summary></member>

nodes.name: formatDate
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>Formats a backend timestamp for display, treating an offset-less ISO string as UTC (the
backend sometimes serializes DateTimeKind.Unspecified values without a 'Z' or offset suffix).
Detects an existing 'Z' or +/-HH:mm offset rather than a bare `.includes('Z')` check, since that
naive check mistakes a `+00:00`-style offset for "no timezone" and appends a second one,
producing "Invalid Date".</summary></member>

nodes.name: blankFieldMapping
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>A neutral starting point for a new scalar-field node's transform config — every FieldMapping
member at its backend default (Connector.Core.DynamicExport.FieldTransform.None /
FieldDataType.String).</summary></member>

nodes.name: columnsAsDisabledScalarFields
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>One disabled scalar-field node per column of `tableName` — the "pick columns via checkbox" UX
shown when a table is selected for the export root or a related entity, shared by
ExportDefinitionEditView.vue (root table) and ExportNodeTreeEditor.vue (nested related tables)
so both populate exactly the same way.</summary></member>

nodes.name: blankRootNode
nodes.doc: <member><summary>An empty root node — the starting tree for a brand-new export definition.</summary></member>

nodes.name: detectExportFile
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>Detects the specific confusion Connector.Infrastructure.ImportNodeWalker.ParseRecords now names
explicitly server-side (its schema_version/schemaVersion branch, added alongside this): a pasted file
carrying "schema_version" (snake_case) but no "schemaVersion" is the connector's own export output
(JsonExportFormatWriter), not an ImportEnvelope — an unrelated shape that happens to share
"records"/"provenance" vocabulary. Returns null for anything else (not JSON, already envelope-shaped,
or some other malformed input) — detection must never guess at a shape it doesn't recognize; an
unrelated parse/shape problem still surfaces through the normal Preview error path.</summary></member>

nodes.name: toImportEnvelope
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>Rewraps a detected export file as a minimal ImportEnvelope: the same records array, the same
provenance block carried through untouched (ImportNodeWalker ignores it entirely — see the regression
test WalkAsync_ProvenanceBlockOnEnvelope_HasNoEffectOnTheWalk), just the wrapper the walker
actually reads. Never touches AllowedWritableColumns or field data — a pure reshape of already-pasted
JSON, not a new trust boundary.</summary></member>

nodes.name: hasIntegrationKeyProvenance
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>True when a detected export's provenance block carries a non-empty integrationKey — the signal that
"Create Import Definition from this export" has anything to work
with. This never claims a match itself: ImportMappingSuggestion.Evaluate still does the real
(IntegrationKey, ContractVersion) lookup server-side once the operator follows through.</summary></member>

nodes.name: blankRootNode
nodes.doc: <member><summary>An empty root node — the starting tree for a brand-new import definition.</summary></member>

nodes.name: collectWritableTargets
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>Every enabled scalar-field TargetColumn the tree currently references, excluding the root match
field — the backend only ever looks for it among the root's direct children
(ImportNodeWalker.FindMatchField) and never treats it as a write target. Feeds
ImportAllowedColumnsEditor.vue's "missing from allowlist" hint, mirroring the recursive collection
ImportDefinitionEndpoints.ValidateNode does server-side.</summary></member>

nodes.name: columnsAsDisabledScalarFields
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>One disabled scalar-field node per column of `tableName` — the same "pick columns via checkbox" UX
ExportNodeTreeEditor.vue gives, shown when a related table is picked for an object/array node.</summary></member>

nodes.name: applyImportMappingSuggestion
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>"Create from export": builds the root node a New
Import Definition starts from once an operator accepts a suggestion. Same starting point as picking the
root table by hand (one disabled scalar-field node per column), except the deterministic root match
field is pre-enabled and correctly keyed to the export's own JSON field name, and every best-effort
candidate field (still unchecked/disabled — the operator must explicitly enable each one) gets its
SourceKey pre-filled so accepting it later is a checkbox, not a retype.</summary></member>

nodes.name: findUnmappedRootFields
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>Best-effort, client-side-only mirror of what ImportNodeWalker.DiffScalarFields actually looks at: for
each record in a pasted ImportEnvelope, only a property whose key equals some enabled scalar-field
child's SourceKey is ever read — any other key on the record is invisible to the walker, no matter what
value it carries. Used solely to warn an operator in ImportDefinitionPreviewPanel.vue that editing such a
key can never move the "changed" count; never sent to the server and never affects what Preview runs.

Returns [] for anything short of a parseable object with a `records` array — malformed/unrelated input
still surfaces through the normal Preview error path, this hint must never guess at it.</summary></member>

nodes.name: RouteAccess
nodes.doc: <member><summary>What a route needs: Admin, or at least one of `anyOf`. A route without this is open to every signed-in user.</summary></member>

nodes.name: findSuggestedRelations
nodes.doc:
<member><summary>FK-based relation suggestions for a given table, in both directions the schema's foreign keys
actually express (see {@link findForwardRelations} and {@link findReverseRelations}). Shared by
the legacy mapping tree (SchemaView.vue, which only wants the reverse/array shape — see its
`.filter(s => s.kind === 'array')`) and the Export Definitions tree builder
(ExportNodeTreeEditor.vue), so both editors detect relations from
one piece of logic instead of two copies drifting apart.</summary></member>

nodes.name: ConnectionView
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Step 1, /connect: the source-system connection form (PostgreSQL, MariaDB or ServiceNow). "Test Connection" validates the form, saves it and reports how many tables the connection exposes; an empty password keeps the one already stored. A 401 ends the session and returns to login. Continues to /source-schema.</summary></member>

nodes.name: DashboardView
nodes.doc: <member><summary>The landing page once a connection is configured (router guard sends first-run visitors to /connect instead) — an orientation point for the areas that used to be reachable only from the account menu, not a replacement for any of them. Counts and tiles appear only for areas the user may open.</summary></member>

nodes.name: ExportDefinitionEditView
nodes.doc: <member><summary>/export-definitions/:id ("new" to create): editor for one export job. Basic fields, the node tree built from the root table's columns, a preview panel and run history; a new job is created first, after which ExportDefinitionRunControls handles save/test/run/duplicate/delete. Without the edit permission a saved job opens read-only.</summary></member>

nodes.name: ExportDefinitionsView
nodes.doc: <member><summary>/export-definitions: the list of export jobs with each job's last run status, plus per-row enable/disable, test run, duplicate and delete (with confirm) — each only for a user holding its permission.</summary></member>

nodes.name: ExportDetail
nodes.doc: <member><summary>/exports/:seqNo: one managed export run: status, a sequence-gap warning when an earlier run wasn't released, and the run details. Offers the next step for its state: four-eyes release, skip (pending or failed runs), or record delivery (released, not yet delivered) — each only with its permission.</summary></member>

nodes.name: ExportView
nodes.doc: <member><summary>/exports ("Managed Export"): the CMDB pipeline's run page. Summarises the active mapping, previews its output, runs an export now in the chosen format (remembered per browser), and lists past runs with links to each run's detail page. Running needs the run permission.</summary></member>

nodes.name: IcdSchemaView
nodes.doc: <member><summary>/icd-schema: read-only reference for the negotiated ICD export contract: the active columns from GET /api/schema, plus ERP fields that are deliberately excluded and why.</summary></member>

nodes.name: ImportDefinitionEditView
nodes.doc: <member><summary>/import-definitions/:id ("new" to create): editor for one import job. Basic fields, the writable-column allowlist, the node tree, a preview of the plan for a pasted sample, and run history. A new job can start from a matching export's suggestion (including a sample handed over via sessionStorage). "Run" stages the sample as a PendingReview run and opens the four-eyes review dialog. Without the edit permission a saved job opens read-only.</summary></member>

nodes.name: ImportDefinitionsView
nodes.doc: <member><summary>/import-definitions: the list of import jobs with each job's last run status, plus per-row enable/disable, duplicate and delete (with confirm) — each only for a user holding its permission.</summary></member>

nodes.name: LoginView
nodes.doc: <member><summary>/login: username/password sign-in. On success it goes to the dashboard, whose route guard sends first-time users without a connection on to /connect.</summary></member>

nodes.name: SchemaView
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Step 3, /export-schema: the legacy single export mapping editor. Pick a source table, then map columns, flattened relations, nested JSON groups and the JSON wrapper; preview the result, load or save presets, and save the mapping that /api/pipeline/run uses. Warns before leaving with unsaved changes. Without the edit permission the mapping and its preview are shown read-only, with no presets or save.</summary></member>

nodes.name: SettingsView
nodes.doc: <member><summary>/settings: the settings forms (managed-export scheduler, GDPR denylist, branding) and this connector's instance identity — each only for a user holding its permission — plus Users and Permissions for Admins.</summary></member>

nodes.name: SourceSchemaView
nodes.doc: <member><summary>/source-schema: browse the connected source's tables and their columns (expand one or all), as introspected from the live connection.</summary></member>

nodes.name: export_customer
nodes.doc: <member><summary>Dedicated to ExportTreeRegressionTests (nested export records assembled in C# from plain rows). Read-only for every test. Covers, in one small graph: several root rows, a 1:1 lookup (order → customer) including a shared parent (orders 100 and 101 → customer 1) and a NULL foreign key (order 102 → no customer), a 1:n relation (order → lines) including an order with none (101), a second nesting level (line → tags) including a line with none (1001), and NULL values in otherwise-populated columns.</summary></member>
